main_text.p: entes, arioli, scientes, diuinantes, magi, siue stylo peritorum vtentes.Deut.18.10.11.Dan.2.2.
Humanæ sunt, quæ fucata humana sapientia nituntur.

Sunt autem qui ea vtuntur, coniectores, qui naturæ certam experientiam fucatè in ijs quæ sunt supra naturam ad probabilem in naturalibus obseruationem imitentur, & de occultis conijciunt, vt qui ex auium volatu, beftiarũq; visceribus, aruspices: vt qui ex nubibus, planetis & astris, planetarij conijcientes dicuntur.Deut.18.12.Dan.2.2.
Diabolicæ sunt, quæ diaboli scientia & arte nituntur.Sunt {Pure diabolicæ, qua vtuntur Pythones. Deut.18.11. {Mixtè diabolicæ.
Pythones, sunt qui impuro spiritu vtuntur ad occulta manifestanda.Leu.19.31. & 20.6. 1.Sam.28.7.8.9. 2.Reg.21.7.Esa.29.4. 1.Sam.28.3.10. 2.Reg.23.4. 1.Chro.10.3. 2.Chro.33.6.Esa.8.18.19.3.
Mixtè diabolicæ, qui alio medio à diabolo edocto nituntur.Deut.18.11.
Necromantia, est qua diabolus mortuorum speciē consulitur.Ibid.
Præstigium, est magia aliqua incerta, aut saltē impia,

page.notes: The brace diagrams are reproduced as outlines; the bracket shapes are approximated. The final line "pia," appears at the right foot of the column and is possibly a catchword-like continuation; it is given as printed. Left-hand page fragments are excluded.
